title: Vehicle occupancy
description: One record: one published average vehicle occupancy (persons per vehicle) for a mode of transport, in a country, year and (where the publisher splits it) trip purpose, exactly as an official or reference dataset publishes it. Voyager use: the trip carbon footprint (turning a per-vehicle factor into a per-passenger one for car, taxi, bus and coach legs) and Local transportation.

mode.description: The mode of transport the occupancy is for (`bus_coach`: buses and coaches together, e.g. the UK's "PSV").

mode_label.description: The publisher's own label path of the row (e.g. "Car / Average Car", "PSV / Total").

trip_purpose.description: The trip purpose the figure is for (`all` = every purpose; `work` = trips in the course of work, i.e. business travel).

time_period.description: The days the figure averages over, when the publisher splits them.

geography.description: Where the figure applies: an English country name, a region the publisher names, or "global".

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code when the figure is for one country.

value.description: The average occupancy exactly as published, in `unit`.

basis.description: How the average is weighted: by distance (person-km per vehicle-km, the figure for per-passenger-km factors) or per vehicle trip.

includes_driver.description: Whether the driver is counted (true: driver plus passengers).

year.description: The year the figure is for, as the publisher states it (e.g. a "2023 values" table).

publisher.description: Who publishes the figure (e.g. "UK Department for Transport (DfT)").

dataset.description: The dataset, table and edition (e.g. "DfT TAG data book, table A1.3.3.2").

source_url.description: The page's own link for this item (official site or detail page), copied verbatim from the page.

as_of.description: The "last updated", "valid from" or publication date the page itself states for this information (YYYY-MM-DD).

items.description: A verbatim quote from the page.

evidence.description: Up to 3 short verbatim quotes from the page that support the most important facts.
